headline: Benchmarking, spectral library and open-search tools for MS-based molecular analysis
label: Mass Spectrometry Analysis Methods
summary: Reanalysis traces a reported PELSA-LiP-MS gap to mismatched conditions, while new MS tools extend library generation and open modification search.
synthesis: The common thread across these preprints is analytical rigor in mass spectrometry-based identification and quantification. A reanalysis of public PELSA and LiP-MS data attributes a reported 21-fold performance gap to mismatched experimental conditions and undisclosed imputation, a benchmarking concern that bears directly on how such comparisons are reported. On the library side, Carafe2 fine-tunes retention time, fragment intensity and ion mobility models on timsTOF DIA data to generate experiment-specific in silico spectral libraries, while a pan-repository effort assembles a 34,222-spectra acylcarnitine MS/MS library from GNPS, MetaboLights and Metabolomics Workbench. MS Andrea scores combinations of PTMs per PSM in open searches, outperforming MSFragger in the reported comparison. What is new is the move beyond delta-mass open searches and generic libraries toward experiment-specific models and combinatorial modification scoring.
